purpose: Compare what a sunflower and a hamster took in over 28 days and how each changed in size
must_show: Sunflower plant
Hamster
Days: 28
Food taken in (g): sunflower 0 g, hamster 560 g
Water taken in: sunflower 50 mL per day, hamster —
Light from window: sunflower 7 hours per day, hamster —
Size change: sunflower Day 0: 12 cm to Day 28: 34 cm; hamster Day 0: 95 g to Day 28: 102 g

purpose: Let the learner name each main part of a flower and point to where it sits on the plant
must_show: A labelled flower with Petal, Stamen, Carpel and Sepal on the flower head
A Stem holding the flower and a Leaf attached to the stem
Each label line points to exactly one part
must_not_show: Roots or soil
Any function text written on the figure

purpose: Show how light, water and carbon dioxide come together inside a leaf to make the sugar the plant uses for growth, and that oxygen leaves the leaf as this happens.
must_show: light reaching the leaf from the Sun
carbon dioxide in the air entering the leaf
water travelling from the roots up the stem into the leaf
water and carbon dioxide combining inside the leaf, driven by light energy, to make sugar, the plant's food
sugar leaving the leaf to be used for growth and stored elsewhere in the plant
oxygen being released from the leaf into the air as the sugar is made
must_not_show: soil supplying food or the material of new growth
the plant taking oxygen in for food-making
chemical formulas or equations

purpose: Show the stages of a frog's life and that the adult lays eggs, which starts the cycle again
must_show: Four stages in a closed loop with arrows: Egg, Tadpole, Young frog, Adult frog
An arrow from Adult frog back to Egg labelled Lays eggs
must_not_show: Any stage not in the list
An arrow running backwards from Egg to Adult frog

purpose: Read how tall a bean plant grew each week and see that the growth was not the same every week
must_show: Four weeks on the horizontal axis: Week 1, Week 2, Week 3, Week 4
Plant height (cm) on the vertical axis
Week 1: 4 cm; Week 2: 9 cm; Week 3: 15 cm; Week 4: 16 cm
Vertical axis label: Height (cm)
must_not_show: Any week beyond Week 4
Any value not in the data

purpose: Compare the resting and after-exercise heart rate of two groups and see which group rose more
must_show: Two groups: Group A and Group B
Two bars for each group: Before exercise and After exercise
Group A: before 72 bpm, after 110 bpm; Group B: before 75 bpm, after 92 bpm
Vertical axis label: Heart rate (bpm)
must_not_show: Any group beyond A and B
A bar drawn to a value not in the data

purpose: Show how muddy water is separated into clear water and solid waste using a filter
must_show: A funnel fitted with filter paper held above a beaker
Muddy water being poured into the funnel
Clear water collecting in the beaker below, with solid residue left on the filter paper
Labels: Funnel, Filter paper, Beaker, Solid residue
must_not_show: A heat source or flame
Any second piece of apparatus

purpose: Show which living things in a pond eat which, so the learner can trace where the energy comes from
must_show: A pond with reeds at the edge
Algae floating in the water
A water snail eating the algae
A small fish eating the snail
A heron standing on the bank eating the fish
Labels: Water snail, Small fish, Heron
must_not_show: Humans or fishing equipment
Any animal not in the food chain

purpose: Locate negative and positive whole numbers on one line and see which of two numbers is greater
must_show: A number line from -5 to 5 with every whole number marked
Point A at -3
Point B at 2
Point C at 5
Zero (0) marked at the centre of the line
must_not_show: Any number beyond -5 or 5
Any decimal point between whole numbers

purpose: Let the learner see that the L-shaped floor is two rectangles whose labeled measurements can be read off, and that the overall width and overall height are not the sides of one rectangle.
must_show: an L-shaped floor plan made from two rectangles
the top edge labelled 8 m
the depth of the top rectangle labelled 3 m
the overall left vertical edge labelled 7 m
the lower rectangle's width labelled 5 m
the bottom-right corner of the enclosing outline that is not part of the floor
must_not_show: any area value or product
the lower rectangle's depth labelled as 4 m, which is to be derived later
the enclosing 8 m by 7 m rectangle drawn as if the floor filled it

purpose: Show the order of three stages in the discovery of penicillin, with the year of each
must_show: A horizontal timeline with three dated stages in order
1928: Fleming notices mould killing bacteria
1941: penicillin first given to a patient
1945: Nobel Prize shared by Fleming, Florey and Chain
1941 stage labelled: First patient treated
must_not_show: Any stage beyond the three shown
Any date not on the timeline

purpose: Sort three materials into conductors and insulators using a small picture of each
must_show: A table with columns Material, Conducts electricity?, and a small picture
Row 1: Copper, Yes, picture of a copper wire
Row 2: Rubber, No, picture of a rubber glove
Row 3: Steel, Yes, picture of a steel spoon
must_not_show: Any material beyond the three rows
Any reason text in the table
